### 1. What the user expresses; simulator behaviour

- Target object: the reefer shipment on booking `AHLU26BGO527604`, container `AHLU5412312`; she asks that "the thawed cartons in container AHLU5412312 [be] added to your claim on this shipment" and wants to know "today whether the line will pay for them".
- Timing: discovery "yesterday, on 13 September"; delivery "on 30 July"; "Nobody saw anything wrong when the cargo was delivered" (loss not apparent at delivery).
- Loss particulars (given when asked): 36 cartons, 720 kg, temperature damage ("thawed and refrozen").
- Authorisation mode: "You are happy for the agent to look up and handle whatever is needed on your account." If told the loss needs its own notice she wants "that notice put in today in any case" and "when the agent sets it up and hands it over you submit it yourself with the details the agent reads back". Amount on the notice: "whatever figure the line's rules put on a notice". If told something else "has to be decided or closed first" she says "the agent should go ahead".
- Simulator stays passive: conveys the need, supplies identity details (phone `+4755527390`, then customer code `AHL-NO-541208`), responds under if/else, runs the user-owned lodging tool only once the agent hands it over, and reads back the claim reference only after submitting. It never states a rule or calculation ("You never tell the agent how a claim should be calculated or decided").

Others: two approved, one rejected, one withdrawn (the withdrawn one is a shortage file on the very container `AHLU5412312`).
- Adding the new loss to a file is excluded: one_container_per_notice "Where a further loss turns up in another container of the shipment, it is never folded into a claim file the cover already holds; it calls for a notice of its own."

### 4. Scored parameters (formula in words, inputs, intermediates, result)

A. Settlement of `6d48f2e5` (CargoCare yardstick — liability_regimes tier card: Total = "CargoCare cover").
- Admissibility checks (all from visible records): kind temperature damage is covered by Total (covered_loss_kinds table); minimum reefer rank 1, container `AHLU5412230` Monitored rank 2 -> covered; logged excursion "no" for Total (temperature_and_delay_loss_conditions); hidden loss window 30 days from 2026-07-30 = 2026-08-29, notice 2026-08-14 in time; time bar 24 months -> 2028-07-30, in time; minimum claim 50.00, 103200.00 not below; no DG acceptance (`find_dg_acceptances` -> none); claimant is the cover holder; documents complete, so no documents-deadline ground; excluded peril — no survey finding is visible through any tool (see counter-proof note).
- Proven loss = amount claimed, capped at the invoice value of the affected packages (proven_loss_and_invoice_value): 412800.00 / 4800 x 240 = 20640.00 (rounded to the cent) < 103200.00 -> proven loss 20640.00.
- Loss basis = proven loss x (1 + 10 %) (cargocare_valuation_uplift, Total 10) = 22704.00 (unrounded).
- Deductible = higher of general (0.00) and temperature (0.00) for Total = 0.00 -> remainder 22704.00.
- CargoCare amount = min(remainder, cap 500000.00) = 22704.00; cap does not bind.
- Aggregate still available on the cover = 2000000.00 − (3784.00 + 6622.00) = 1989594.00 (both approvals fewer than 12 whole months before today) -> does not reduce.
- Final amount rounded to the cent: 22704.00; measure `proven_loss` (final_settlement_amount_and_measure: "proven loss: all remaining cases, a proven loss that was itself held to the invoice value of the packages affected among them").
- Desk authority Total 50000.00 -> 22704.00 is within (desk_settlement_authority).

B. Notice amount for the new notice on `AHLU5412312` (container_value_at_risk + notice_amount_container_cap): declared cargo value 412800.00 / booking container count 4 = 103200.00; Total cap 500000.00 not exceeded -> 103200.00. Other notice fields as the claimant states them: `temperature_damage`, `damage_apparent_at_delivery=false`, 36 packages, 720.0 kg.

C. Rejection reason of the new notice: rank 1 (103200.00 not below 50.00) no; rank 2 (temperature damage covered by Total; `AHLU5412312` Standard rank 1 >= minimum 1) no; rank 3 (time bar 2028-07-30) no; rank 4 hidden loss window 2026-07-30 + 30 = 2026-08-29, notice 2026-09-14 later -> holds. Reason `notice_out_of_time`.

The customer is told the new loss will not be paid, with the reason, and that the earlier claim was approved at its amount. No settlement payment tool exists in the KB; payment of the approved amount is not a desk step on this call.

### 6. Problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

Root problem P0: the customer wants the thawed cartons in `AHLU5412312` paid, "added to your claim".

- P0 -> P1 (the loss needs its own notice, lodged by the customer). Basis: one_container_per_notice "it is never folded into a claim file the cover already holds; it calls for a notice of its own"; notice_of_loss_lodging "This tool belongs to the customer … the agent does not run it on the customer's behalf"; claimants_and_claim_count "nobody else, the desk included, lodges it on the claimant's behalf". This is the root policy's own rule, not an inter-problem hop. Mark: **read off** (stated as a rule; also restated in successive_claims_on_one_cover "That further loss has to be notified separately").
- P1 -> P2 (the notice cannot be registered while the cover is occupied; the open claim must first leave the open state). Combination: one_container_per_notice lodging conditions "the cover has no claim open" + record `status: claim_open` and file `6d48f2e5` at `documents_complete`; claimants_and_claim_count "A cover never has more than one claim open at the same time". Mark: **read off** — one_container_per_notice §"A cover with an open claim": "the cover stays shut to any further notice until the claim is decided or withdrawn" states the waiting relation outright; successive_claims_on_one_cover "The further notice therefore relies on the cover having been returned to the closed-claim state by the closure of the decided earlier claim" states it again.
- P2 -> P3 (the way the open claim leaves: decision by approval at 22704.00, not withdrawal, not rejection). Combination: record_state clause 1 (claim open + documents complete admit approval); no visible rejection ground (item 4A); withdrawal is the claimant's act ("The claimant may withdraw a claim that is open") and no withdrawal tool is published, while the customer wants to be paid; desk authority covers the amount. Amount derived hop by hop (item 4A). Mark: amount **derived**; the choice "approve" is **read off** — successive_claims_on_one_cover "The desk decides the earlier claim by approving its settlement" and "for a claim whose documents are complete it is the approval entry that constitutes the decision".
- P3 -> P4 (after the decision, close the claim on the cover, so the cover reaches `claim_closed`). Combination: approve tool "leaves the cover's status as it was" (still claim_open); settlement_payment_and_claim_closure "Once a claim has been decided … the open claim on the cover is closed"; claimants_and_claim_count "Notice of loss opens a claim on a cover whose status is active, or on a cover whose earlier claim has been closed". Mark: **read off** — claim_closure_on_cover "a cover in that state can take notice of a further loss on the same shipment" and successive_claims_on_one_cover (closure relied on by the further notice) state the enabling link directly.
- P4 -> P1 executes (customer lodges; count 4 < 5 ceiling; claimant is holder; no claim open) -> P5 (the registered notice is rejected at once, reason by rank). Combination: ranking_of_immediate_rejection_grounds + notice_window_rules + notice_periods_by_tier + delivery date on the cover + notice date on the file; registered_notice_particulars (grounds tested on the notice-registered file only). The ground identity (`notice_out_of_time`) is **derived**; that the further notice will be rejected rather than left waiting for documents is **read off** — successive_claims_on_one_cover "its notice fails one of the grounds settled at the moment of registration" and "the further notice on file … rejected with its controlled reason"; one_container_per_notice Points of judgement "A notice would be rejected at once for arriving outside its notice period. That is not a reason to refuse registration" names exactly this task's ground.
- P5 -> P6 (close the rejected claim). Combination: settlement_payment_and_claim_closure closure rule; claim_closure_on_cover tool (object "a cover whose open claim has been decided, whether by approval … or by rejection"). Mark: **read off** — successive_claims_on_one_cover "closes each claim once it has been decided, so that closing happens twice" and "Closing the further notice likewise acts on a decided claim, so it relies on the rejection of that notice".

Resulting list and order: approve `6d48f2e5` -> close cover -> customer lodges new notice -> reject it (`notice_out_of_time`) -> close cover. Dependencies: lodging depends on closure, closure depends on decision; rejection depends on registration; second closure depends on rejection. Every hop is also independently derivable by combination (bases quoted above); but every inter-problem hop is also stated outright in successive_claims_on_one_cover, and P1->P2 / P3->P4 are further stated in one_container_per_notice and claim_closure_on_cover.

### Two-way counter-proof

- Support: every value and action above rests on a quoted KB sentence plus a tool return; the full sequence replays through rt_query to the terminal state stated in item 5.
- "Do only what the customer asked" (add the cartons to a claim / just lodge a notice): excluded by one_container_per_notice (no folding into an existing file) and by the lodging condition "the cover has no claim open" against the record `claim_open`; a notice lodged without deciding and closing `6d48f2e5` is "not registered at all" per one_container_per_notice, so the customer's request would get no answer on record.
- Closest alternatives excluded:
  - Withdraw `6d48f2e5` instead of deciding it: withdrawal is the claimant's act and no tool publishes it; the file is ready for decision and payable.
  - Reject `6d48f2e5`: no ground holds on its records (item 4A).
  - Measure `aggregate_limit` or `cover_limit`: available aggregate 1989594.00 and cap 500000.00 both exceed 22704.00.
  - Proven loss = claimed 103200.00: excluded by proven_loss_and_invoice_value cap at invoice value of affected packages (20640.00).
  - Lodge directly after approval without closing: cover would still read `claim_open` (approve tool "leaves the cover's status as it was").
  - Notice amount = customer's own figure or insured-value basis (454080/4 = 113520.00): excluded — the BL value and booking container count are both on record, so container_value_at_risk's first row applies; the customer offers no figure.
  - Leave the new notice waiting for documents: excluded, rank-4 ground holds and immediate grounds are decided on registration.
  - Rejection reason `not_covered_by_tier` (Standard reefer on `AHLU5412312`): excluded, Total's minimum reefer rank is 1 and Standard is rank 1.
  - Consider the withdrawn shortage file on `AHLU5412312`: withdrawn, excluded from count and from any decision.
- Residual visibility note (not affecting the answer): the excluded-peril ground rests on "the survey report that the claims department has recorded" (misdeclared_cargo_and_excluded_perils), and no runtime finder exposes survey findings; the claim file shows only `outcome`. The blind reader concludes "no finding visible, so no exclusion" — to be checked against the source in gt_comparison.

### Finding R0-1 — the whole problem tree of this task is laid out in one document (aggregation)

- Symptom: a solver can follow `doc_claims_successive_claims_on_one_cover_963064de` hop by hop without discovering any hop.
- Root cause: the workflow's scenario and `order_rationale` were rendered as a statement of the governed situation, the end state, the parts of each party and "What each part relies on", instead of being carried only by the definitions and principles they follow from.
- Evidence (document `successive_claims_on_one_cover_963064de`):
  - §"The situation governed": "any cargo cover whose earlier claim remains open, with complete documents, at the time the claimant reports a further loss discovered in a different container of the same delivered shipment. That further loss has to be notified separately, and its notice fails one of the grounds settled at the moment of registration." — this is task 0's opening state and the outcome of the rejection hop.
  - §"The parties and their parts": "The desk decides the earlier claim by approving its settlement, decides the further notice by rejecting it with its controlled reason, and closes each claim once it has been decided, so that closing happens twice." — the full action list.
  - §"What each part relies on": four bullets giving closure <- decision, approval <- claim open, further notice <- closure ("The further notice therefore relies on the cover having been returned to the closed-claim state by the closure of the decided earlier claim"), rejection <- registration ("The rejection therefore relies on the further notice having been registered"), second closure <- rejection — i.e. both declared `prerequisite` edges (`claims_ext_notice_container_value` -> `claims_ext_settlement_invoice_share`, `claims_ext_lodging_rejection_grounds` -> `claims_ext_notice_container_value`) plus the workflow order, in one place.
- Nature: each hop is individually correct and each is also derivable elsewhere in the corpus (blind item 6), so the solution is unchanged; the defect is that the chain is readable off one page, which the skill lists as a KB-RUNTIME RED ("the visible KB aggregates the prerequisite chain"). The source layer does carry the whole order in one field (the workflow's `order_rationale`), so this is not an addition without a source (see policy_kb/0.md kb_to_source); it is a rendering that states what the source intends to be entailed. The same evidence is scored under KB-EXPLICIT as E0-1.
- Affected: `doc_claims_successive_claims_on_one_cover_963064de`, all three sections.
